items.stem: ‘The Depression was the main reason for the Nazi rise to power.’ Discuss.

items.stem: ‘Hitler's consolidation of power in 1933-34 was a legal revolution.’ How far do you agree with this view?
items.answer: For: Hitler was appointed constitutionally. The Enabling Act was passed by the Reichstag with the required two-thirds majority. Decrees were issued under Article 48. Against: Communist deputies were excluded and SA men intimidated the Reichstag. Terror against opponents in 1933. The Night of the Long Knives was murder outside the law. Judgement: the revolution used legal forms, but it rested on terror and intimidation, so "legal" describes its appearance rather than its reality.

items.stem: How important was the Enabling Act in the creation of the Nazi dictatorship?
items.answer: For: It gave Hitler legislative power without the Reichstag. It provided the legal basis for later measures. It ended parliamentary government. Against: The Reichstag Fire Decree had already suspended civil rights. Gleichschaltung and terror mattered as much. Control of the army was secured only in 1934. Judgement: the Enabling Act was the legal foundation of the dictatorship, but it was one step in a process that also depended on terror and the army.

items.stem: Historians have offered several reasons why unemployment fell rapidly in Nazi Germany. A: Women and Jews were removed from the figures. B: Recovery from the Depression was already under way. C: Rearmament and conscription from 1935. Which was the most significant? Explain your answer with reference to the other reasons.
items.answer: Any reasoned choice. A: Women and Jews were removed from the figures. B: Recovery from the Depression was already under way. C: Rearmament and conscription from 1935. Possible judgement: rearmament and public works created jobs, but the figures were also massaged.

items.stem: How successful was Nazi economic policy, 1933-39?
items.answer: For: Unemployment fell from about 6 million to under half a million. Rapid rearmament. Recovery of industrial output. Against: Autarky targets were missed. Living standards and consumer goods suffered (guns versus butter). By 1939 the economy faced shortages and overheating. Judgement: it achieved recovery and rearmament, but by 1939 it was unbalanced and not ready for a long war.

items.stem: Hitler was appointed Chancellor by President Hindenburg on 30 January 1933. Analyse the reasons why Hitler was appointed Chancellor in January 1933.
items.answer: Papen and Hindenburg's advisers believed they could control him. Schleicher had lost Hindenburg's confidence. The Nazis were the largest party, so their support was needed for a majority. Elites wanted mass support for authoritarian government. Judgement: Hitler came to power through a backstairs deal by conservatives who wanted to use his mass support.

items.stem: Mateo is planning an answer to the question: “‘The Depression was the main reason for the Nazi rise to power.’ How far do you agree?” Write a one-sentence line of argument for the answer and outline two points Mateo could use to support the view and two to challenge it.
items.answer: Line of argument: the Depression made the Nazis a mass party, but Hitler became Chancellor because conservative elites chose to bring him in. items.stem: Lucas is planning an answer to the question: “‘The Nazi regime created a genuine Volksgemeinschaft.’ How far do you agree?” Write a one-sentence line of argument for the answer and outline two points Lucas could use to support the view and two to challenge it.
items.answer: Line of argument: the regime created a sense of national community for many "Aryan" Germans, but it was built on exclusion and coercion rather than genuine equality. items.stem: Study all the sources. Source A: a report by an SPD underground observer (Sopade), 1936 (summary). The reports noted that many workers were glad to have jobs and enjoyed KdF trips, but grumbled about long hours, low wages and food prices. Source B: a Nazi poster advertising the KdF car, 1938 (description). The poster shows a family in a shiny Volkswagen on an autobahn, with the slogan "Save five marks a week if you want your own car!" “The Nazi regime created a genuine Volksgemeinschaft.” How far do Sources A and B support this view?
items.answer: Source A challenges: it shows grumbling and divisions. Evaluation: observers were opponents of the regime and might emphasise discontent. Source B supports: it shows the regime presenting a community of shared prosperity. Evaluation: it is propaganda; very few savers ever received a car. Grouping: support B; challenge A.
